participantInstructions: The event will be presented to you through your reading of the 21st Century Skills, Performance Indicators and Event Situation. You will be evaluated on how well you demonstrate the 21st Century Skills and meet the performance indicators of this event. Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are the general manager of TABLETOP COMMONS, a board game cafe that sells coffee, small plates and table time inside a lending library of roughly eight hundred games. Four months ago TABLETOP COMMONS bought a smaller rival, GAME NIGHT LOUNGE, and the two shops still run on separate menus, separate schedules and separate habits. The owner (judge) wants that settled before the busy winter season.

What the two shops actually sell is not the games. It is the game guides, staff trained to read a table, pick a title that fits the people sitting at it, and teach the rules in under ten minutes. Guides are the reason families who have never played anything past checkers stay for three hours. Guides are also the most expensive line on the schedule and the hardest role to hire for.

In March a new cafe, DICE AND DINE, opened six blocks away with a similar library and lower prices. Meanwhile the unfinished merger has TABLETOP COMMONS paying for two of everything. Your assistant manager has costed out a fix that solves both problems: retire the guide role, put printed rule cards and short tutorial videos on every table, and run both shops on smaller, cheaper crews.

The savings are real and would cover what the merger still owes. They would also remove the one thing DICE AND DINE cannot copy quickly, and the guides who came over from GAME NIGHT LOUNGE were promised their hours through the end of the year. Keeping the guides on every shift honors that promise and holds the regulars, but leaves prices above the new cafe's and the two payrolls uncombined.

The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend whether to retire the guide role or keep the guides on every shift, and to explain what each choice does to the reason customers pick this cafe over another. The owner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of TABLETOP COMMONS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You bought GAME NIGHT LOUNGE four months ago and you have not finished folding it in. You want the general manager's recommendation on whether to retire the guide role in favor of rule cards and tutorial videos, or to keep the guides on every shift, and you want to hear what the choice does to why customers come.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If you had recommended the other course, what would it have cost us?
What would we have gained from it that your recommendation gives up?
